title: Economics
description: Economics (Group II) for ICSE Examination Years 2027 and 2028: production, demand and supply, markets, banking, inflation and consumer awareness.

syllabusBaselines.source: CISCE Research, Development and Curriculum Division, Economics syllabus, Examination Year 2028 (reproduced); cross-checked against the Oswal, Shaalaa and Jagran Josh 2026-27 listings, which give the same six units.
syllabusBaselines.note: Verified October 2026. Six prescribed units, with public finance taught inside the banking unit. This is the Group II Economics paper (80 marks, 2 hours, 20 marks internal assessment) and is a different subject from the Group III Economic Applications paper; the regulations forbid taking both.

sections.title: Economics
sections.description: Six prescribed units from production to consumer awareness.

chapters.title: The Productive Mechanism
chapters.blurb: Land, labour, capital and the entrepreneur: their characteristics, productivity and role in production and development.

chapters.title: Theory of Demand and Supply
chapters.blurb: The laws of demand and supply, schedules and curves, shifts against movements and the elasticity of each.

chapters.title: Market
chapters.blurb: Perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition and oligopoly: features, examples and the differences between them.

chapters.title: Banking in India
chapters.blurb: Money and its functions, commercial banks and credit creation, central bank functions, monetary policy and demonetisation.

chapters.title: Public Finance
chapters.blurb: Public revenue, direct and indirect taxation and GST, public expenditure and the meaning and types of public debt.

chapters.title: Inflation
chapters.blurb: WPI and CPI, the stages of inflation, demand-pull against cost-push causes and its effects on different income groups.

chapters.title: Consumer Awareness
chapters.blurb: How consumers are exploited, their rights and duties, COPRA and the RTI, food adulteration and the PDS, BIS, AGMARK and ECOMARK schemes.

sections.paperLabel: ICSE Class X · Theory + Internal Assessment
